speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: We regularly review and update the CPF system.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: The first two sets of amendments in the Bill, which effect the closure of the SA for members aged 55 and above and the expansion of the HPS, are part of the evolution of the CPF system to continue serving the needs of Singaporeans.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: The closure of the SA has been discussed at length in this House since it was announced at Budget this year.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: As I had earlier explained during the 2024 Committee of Supply debate for the Ministry of Manpower (MOM), the principle behind closing the SA for members aged 55 and above is to right-site CPF monies.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: Only CPF savings committed towards long-term retirement needs should earn the higher long-term interest rate.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: Today, members aged 55 and above have four CPF accounts: one, the Ordinary Account (OA); two, the MediSave Account (MA); three, the SA; as well as four, the Retirement Account (RA).

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: CPF members will be notified when their SA is closed, through a hard copy notification, as well as an email or SMS where applicable.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: As per the current practice for members turning 55 today, members' SA savings will be transferred to the RA, up to the Full Retirement Sum (FRS) applicable to their cohort.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: The savings in the RA will continue to earn the higher long-term interest rate, which is currently at 4.14%.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: With the closure of the SA, any remaining SA savings will be transferred to the OA and can be withdrawn.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: Members who wish to commit their withdrawable savings to their long-term retirement needs can opt to transfer their OA savings to their RA up to the Enhanced Retirement Sum (ERS).

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: As Members of the House would know, CPF members can then choose to start receiving their RA savings as monthly retirement payouts anytime from the age of 65 to 70.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: In gist, the SA closure will not prevent members from earning the higher long-term interest rate.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: They can do so by voluntarily transferring their savings to the RA, up to the prevailing ERS.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: But if members want to retain the flexibility to withdraw these savings at any time, then the savings can remain in the OA and earn the OA interest rate.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: The Bill will permit the Board to implement the SA closure and the necessary related actions, such as transferring members' SA savings into their RA and OA.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: Next, I will speak about the expansion of the HPS.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: The HPS is an insurance scheme that protects CPF members and their loved ones from losing their Housing and Development Board (HDB) flats in the event of the member's death, terminal illness or total permanent disability.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: Today, members are covered at a standard premium rate if they are assessed to be generally in good health, even if they have pre-existing health conditions.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: However, around 1.3%, or about 1,400 HPS applicants, are rejected annually due to pre-existing health conditions based on factors, such as overall severity, prognosis, control of the health condition and the member's health risk profile.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: In line with industry practices, these members will pay higher premiums that are commensurate with the higher likelihood of claims.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: Even with this premium loading for such members, the HPS would provide coverage at one of the lowest premiums that such members would pay in the current market.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: For members who are eligible for coverage today, there will be no premium loading and no change to the standard premium rate.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: To ensure that the HPS remains sustainable and affordable for the majority of members, the small minority of members with more severe health conditions, such as those currently receiving treatment for cancer, would not be able to participate in HPS.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: This is also in line with industry practice.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: Nevertheless, CPF members who face financial difficulties in repaying their mortgage loans can approach HDB for further assistance.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: The expansion of HPS will be implemented from mid-2025.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: For those offered coverage with premium loading, participation will be on an opt-in basis.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: We will assess any future developments to industry practice in our regular review of the CPF system.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: Taken together, the closure of the SA and the expansion of the HPS coverage to more members with pre-existing health conditions will evolve our CPF system to better serve the needs of Singaporeans over the course of their lives.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: The remaining four amendments are to streamline the administration of the CPF Board and CPF schemes.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: The amendments give the Minister the discretion to appoint a Deputy Chairperson from amongst the Board members.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: This is in line with common practices across other Statutory Boards.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: There will be no change to the maximum number of 15 Board members.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: The Board currently comprises a Chairperson, a Deputy Chairperson, six tripartite representatives and seven other persons.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: Excluding the Chairperson and the CEO of CPF Board, the Minister may now appoint a Deputy Chairperson from any of the remaining Board members with the President’s concurrence.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: CPF Board will continue to operate efficiently with this change.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: I will now move on to the next amendment.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: Currently, when members sell their property, their sales proceeds are distributed in a specific order.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: For example, a member with an HDB loan would have to repay any outstanding property tax, outstanding HDB loan and resale levies, before refunding the amount of CPF savings used in the purchase of the property including accrued interest.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: As implemented by the Ministry of National Development and HDB starting from the October 2024 Build-To-Order (BTO) exercise, there is a New Flat Classification Framework which will classify new flats as Standard, Plus and Prime based on locational attributes.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: This new framework will help to achieve three important objectives: one, it keeps home ownership affordable; two, it maintains a good social mix; and three, it keeps the system of public housing subsidies fair for everyone.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: To ensure affordability, Plus and Prime flats come with additional subsidies to enable a wider range of Singaporeans to purchase them.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: This is on top of significant market discounts that are applied to all BTO flats today.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: And to ensure fairness for everyone, these additional subsidies will be recovered upon the sale of the flats.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: The recovery of additional subsidies will be done before the required CPF housing refund is made to the member's CPF account.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: This maintains parity with other flat buyers who did not receive these additional subsidies and is important to preserve the fairness of our public housing subsidies.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: We will also amend the Act to clarify that the CPF Board requires CPF refunds only upon property disposal and not at the point of transactions, which involve the issuance of a new lease or title without any changes to the ownership of the property.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: Such transactions include the purchase of recess areas outside of one's HDB flat and lease extensions.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: Some members today also provide undertakings to pledge their property to CPF Board, to access more funds in their RA for immediate use.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: In some cases, new co-owners could be added after the existing owner had pledged the property.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: The amendments clarify that CPF Board also requires new co-owners to refund the pledged monies to the existing owner's CPF accounts, upon disposal of the property.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: Lastly, we will remove provisions that were previously included to support the CPF Job Record Scheme and which are no longer relevant today.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: In the past, employers could request for CPF Board to share prospective employees’ employment history under the CPF Job Record Scheme.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: This scheme was terminated in 1983 and CPF Board has not shared any prospective employees' employment history with employers since then.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: As such, we will amend the CPF Act to remove this provision.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: (In Mandarin):   The Government regularly reviews and updates the CPF system to ensure it continues to meet the needs of Singaporeans at different stages of life.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: Previously, we announced the closure of the SA for CPF members aged 55 and above.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: We will notify affected members by letter, as well as an email or SMS.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: After the SA has been closed, the savings in it will be transferred to the RA up to the FRS.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: These savings will continue to earn higher long-term interest rates.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: If a member's RA has already reached the FRS, the remaining savings in the SA will be transferred to their OA and can be withdrawn at any time.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: Members can also choose to transfer the savings from their OA to the RA up to the ERS.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: This way, members can earn a higher interest rate and receive higher retirement income.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: This means that currently, over 99% of the affected members will be able to transfer all their SA savings to the RA.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: The Government will also expand the coverage of the HPS from mid-2025.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: Members with certain pre-existing conditions that are not so severe, such as certain types of stroke and heart disorder, will be able to get coverage.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: Even if they are required to pay a higher premium, the premium will still be amongst the lowest in the current market.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: We will assess any future developments to industry practice in our regular reviews of the CPF system.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: We will also streamline the administration of the CPF Board and the CPF schemes.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: The overall revisions will ensure that the CPF system, as an important pillar of our country's social security system, can continue to meet the needs of Singaporeans. : Sir, let me conclude.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: All in all, this ensures that the CPF system continues to serve the needs of Singaporeans over the course of their lives and to continue to remain effective as a key pillar of Singapore's social security system.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: I have three points of clarification to raise.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: My first point is on the closure of the SA for members 55 years old and above.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Can the Minister explain what it intends these circumstances to be?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: The closure of the SA was the subject of extensive discussion during the Committee of Supply debates earlier this year.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: It has also been the subject of much discussion by the general public.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: The policy is understandably of significant concern for some Singaporeans who have to reconsider their retirement nest eggs.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: CPF members may top up or transfer savings from their OA to SA to enjoy higher interest rates while building a retirement sum enough to enjoy the highest possible monthly payouts in retirement.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: This results in a higher-yielding SA that can be withdrawn on demand after they turn 55.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: I am heartened to see that there have been numerous explainers by both the CPF Board and the Government to clarify the rationale for the changes.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: But the reality remains that some CPF members will need to re-evaluate their retirement strategies.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Can the CPF Board and the Government share what steps and resources will be extended to members to help them navigate the impact of this new policy on their personal retirement plans?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Can the Government also share how many members are expected to be able to reach the FRS following the top-up from the SA?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: This milestone is significant to members because after it is reached, the balance in the SA will go to the OA.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: In 2022, the CPF Board shared that they expect about eight in 10 active CPF members turning 55 in 2027 to be able to set aside at least the BRS.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Moving forward, will the Government regularly share the number of members expected to reach the BRS, FRS and the ERS?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: My second point is on how the changes to the HPS will impact current members with pre-existing conditions.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Currently, the CPF Board already has the power under section 31(2) of the CPF Act to allow a person who is not in good health to join the HPS.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Such a person must apply to the CPF Board to join the HPS.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: The CPF Board may impose conditions, such as requiring medical examinations and disclosure of health information.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Can the Minister share if there are members who are not in good health but are already covered under the HPS under the section 31(2) exception?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: For these members, will the amendments affect the terms and conditions to which they are currently subject to?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: My third and final point is on the members with pre-existing conditions who are not currently under the HPS.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: The explanatory statement states that the amendments are intended to permit persons with "certain serious health conditions" to join the HPS, subject to premium loading.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Will there be an exhaustive list of these "certain serious health conditions" that the Ministry will use to include or exclude individuals from the HPS going forward?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Given that the basis for their rejection may now be re-evaluated, will such applicants be notified that they can submit a new application to be considered again?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: It would be a shame if the expansion of the HPS fails to benefit seriously ill segments of the population purely because they were unaware that their rejection could be reconsidered.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Notwithstanding these clarifications, I stand in support of this Bill.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: I suspend the Sitting and will take the Chair at 4.25 pm.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: Sitting accordingly suspended at 4.08 pm until 4.25 pm.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: I will focus my comments on the clauses relating to prioritising the recovery of subsidies following the sale of flats and those pertaining to the closure of the SAs.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: While I support the Bill, I have concerns over these two aspects.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: I believe this is to accommodate the larger subsidies that are likely to be extended for Plus and Prime flats.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: The notion of repaying what one owes is, on its face, unobjectionable.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: That said, I believe many of us in this House have had residents appeal for consideration of higher mortgage loans because they cannot afford the cash outlay.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: This could lead to a disconnect: those selling a flat would now be required to fork out a cash amount, so as to pay off the subsidies but, in doing so, they exhaust much of any cash gains that were made from the sale of the flat.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: Yet, they could still well face a gap between the market price of their next resale flat versus its official valuation, which would have to be made up with cash on hand.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: I have had residents in Sengkang face such a dilemma when they seek not even to upgrade, but to downgrade, and I am certain that they are not alone.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: At present, HDB appears to be dealing with this issue on a case-by-case basis, accepting appeals that occasionally enfold additional amounts into the HDB Flat Eligibility (HFE) mortgage loan.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: But the bases for HDB decisions are opaque and, more importantly, I believe I have raised what amounts to a systemic issue that should merit more careful study by HDB.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: Another key thrust of this Bill addressed by clauses 2 through 16 is to impose institutional reforms that would put an end to CPF “shielding".

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: This practice, which allows the hiving off of SA funds from being transferred into the RA, thereby accruing higher returns while also enjoying higher liquidity, had become so widespread that websites and financial institutions were openly advising on how to pursue the practice.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: It got to a stage where one could legitimately wonder if the Government was at least tacitly endorsing this CPF hack.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: Perhaps more troubling, it appeared to have been a loophole exploited by those who were somewhat better-off and financially more sophisticated.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: After all, ensuring that there would be sufficient excess funds in the OA to make up for any BRS shortfall during the transfer window would only be possible if one had larger CPF balances to begin with.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: This strategy would also typically be known to those who ran in more financially-informed circles or, at least, had access to a savvy financial advisor.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: However, I believe it is worthwhile making a few additional points.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: First, we should understand why, beyond the notion of fairness mentioned earlier, this loophole was ultimately unsustainable from a purely financial perspective.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: Sustaining an interest-bearing SA after the age of 55 would have meant savings that combined both higher interest rates relative to the OA, with comparable liquidity.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: Yet there is almost always an inherent tradeoff between higher returns and these returns being locked into an investment for a longer duration.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: This is fairly standard stuff in financial economics.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: Pension managers, such as CPF, would not have been exempt from this tradeoff and their allocations to more illiquid investments is what, in part, would have allowed them to harness the higher returns necessary to meet SA obligations.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: That said, there is at least some degree to which we need to acknowledge that closing the loophole amounts to an upending of both account holders' expectations, as well as the legacy rights of those who invested in the SA prior to this Bill.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: This is, of course, yet another reprise of the theme of retrospective lawmaking, which is something that both my hon friend Louis Chua, as well as I, have raised in this House on prior occasions.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: In this instance, it is the notion that those who will now experience disruptions to their retirement planning, since they had originally planned on having SA income as part of their retirement portfolio, need not be compensated.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: But as mentioned earlier, there was little indication that what they were doing was either inappropriate or illegal.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: To be clear, those who invested in the SA have, undeniably, enjoyed the higher rates associated with locking their balances in that account in the meantime.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: In fairness, it was always known that there would be a transfer of SA funds into the RA at the age of 55.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: Still, there are at least some who would have been hurt by this change in policy.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: Hence, while calling for outright compensation for this group may be a step too far, it seems at least fair to acknowledge that some have been, at the very least, inadvertent victims in the Government's policy shift and to ask how they may be able to receive guidance on how to go forward.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: Perhaps, more fundamentally, we should also ask the question of what drove so many to seek to squeeze higher returns in the first place.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: I am hopeful that CPF Board will continue to extend options for our account holders to build up sufficient savings for retirement.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: One useful reform, which admittedly goes beyond the pure scope of the Bill but is consistent with its spirit, is to offer more options for higher returns.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: Decades of research has shown that these are among the most appealing ways to build retirement wealth.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: Rather than continue to indirectly encourage the overweighting of real estate in our retirement portfolios, we should ensure that equities which tend to offer even higher returns, on average, over the long run, feature prominently for future generations' CPF savings.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: This could even have a secondary spillover effect, bolstering our moribund stock exchange.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: Rather, I hope to highlight how many Singaporeans feel that their rate of accumulation of CPF savings is less and less able to keep up with their retirement needs.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: Some of this has led to pathologies, such as a stretch for yield in exploiting the SA loophole.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: Others have tried to parlay the HDB housing ladder, but this effort runs up against the goal of keeping public housing more affordable.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: This is further exacerbated by how extracting cash from a housing investment may be more challenging than sometimes believed, as I explained earlier on in my speech.

speaker: Ms See Jinli Jean (Nominated Member)
text: Except for HDB owners with serious pre-existing illnesses, HPS insures CPF members until the age of 65 or until the housing loans are paid up.

speaker: Ms See Jinli Jean (Nominated Member)
text: Nonetheless, I would like to seek clarification on three areas.

speaker: Ms See Jinli Jean (Nominated Member)
text: What about those who were previously rejected by HPS and are now under private mortgage insurance?

speaker: Ms See Jinli Jean (Nominated Member)
text: Second, in the same Parliamentary Question response, the Minister had cited the affordability of premiums across all HPS policyholders and the financial viability of the scheme as considerations when reviewing the coverage of HPS.

speaker: Ms See Jinli Jean (Nominated Member)
text: In this regard, how does the expansion of the insured base impact the premium for members in the medium term?

speaker: Ms See Jinli Jean (Nominated Member)
text: Could the Minister explain the process by which the Board determines the health risk threshold and the frequency by which this threshold would be reviewed?

speaker: Ms See Jinli Jean (Nominated Member)
text: For members who must bear premium loading, what is the process and frequency for the Board to review these members' assessed risk and their premium loading payable?

speaker: Ms See Jinli Jean (Nominated Member)
text: How does the Board determine the premium loading amount and would the amount vary from individual-to-individual and from year-to-year?

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Imagine a family's breadwinner is suddenly struck by illness or disability.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: The breadwinner can no longer provide, medical bills start piling up and anxiety sets in.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: In these difficult times, the last thing anyone should fear is losing their home.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Yet, for many families, this fear becomes a reality when health crises strike unexpectedly.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: The proposed expansion of HPS is a significant step toward addressing this concern.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: It offers a critical safety net for residents, helping them to manage the financial responsibilities of home ownership, especially in light of rising costs and uncertain circumstances.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: While I support this initiative, I seek clarity on several aspects to ensure these provisions truly protect the financial well-being of our residents, without creating unintended burdens.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: While I understand the need for financial viability, this amendment risks increasing costs for those least able to bear them.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Premium loading based solely on health risks could be seen as penalising residents for becoming ill.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: I urge the Minister to explain the rationale behind this measure and, more importantly, how will it impact low-income and elderly residents who are already grappling with healthcare expenses?

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Second, Mr Speaker, Sir, I worry that this policy may disproportionately affect individuals with pre-existing conditions and those from lower-income groups.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: What safeguards are in place to prevent this?

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: How will the Ministry ensure a balance between the scheme's financial sustainability and maintaining affordability and accessibility for all, regardless of health status?

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: I also urge the Government to consider the broader implications.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Will premium loading inadvertently leave those who need protection the most without adequate coverage?

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: We must not allow a policy designed to provide security to end up creating new challenges.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: By the time HPS is needed, how many members will have had to dip into their CPF to pay off their loans?

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Third, Mr Speaker, Sir, I call on the Minister to ensure transparency in how premiums are adjusted, as stated in section 32A(3).

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: This is critical to avoid arbitrary decisions, especially when it comes to reducing premiums for residents whose health improves.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: A clear and understandable framework will foster trust and fairness.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: How frequently will CPF Board review these premiums and how will such reviews be communicated to members?

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Fourth, Mr Speaker, Sir, I seek clarity on the types of conditions that will be covered under the expanded scheme.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: The inclusion of individuals with serious pre-existing conditions is commendable.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: However, I ask for more clarity on the conditions that will be covered and how these assessments will be made.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: I understand that eligibility is not based on a predefined list of conditions.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: They are the unfortunate realities faced by many of our residents.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Some cancers detected and treated early pose a low risk of recurrence.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Similarly, stroke patients who have been treated and have recovered well are less likely to experience another stroke.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Should not these patients, who are now relatively healthy, be reconsidered for inclusion?

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Who will be on the medical review board making these decisions?

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Can individuals undergoing treatment for common age related conditions, or those at risk of developing them, expect to be covered under the expanded HPS?

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Just as important, how will we communicate the eligibility criteria to the public in a transparent and easily understood way?

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Clarity is essential to avoid disappointment and to ensure residents can rely on the protection that HPS promises.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: In closing, Mr Speaker, Sir, while the intent behind these policy changes is commendable, we must commit to transparency and clear communication.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: When premiums increase, we must be prepared to explain why and show how these changes will bring tangible benefits.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: We must also outline the support available for those who struggle with higher premiums, such as subsidies, payment plans, or alternative solutions.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Most importantly, we need to ensure that safeguards are in place to prevent undue burdens and provide fair access for all Singaporeans, regardless of their financial situation.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: With these commitments, I believe this Bill can enhance the well-being of all Singaporeans.

speaker: Mr Neil Parekh Nimil Rajnikant (Nominated Member)
text: For Singaporeans, particularly those entering their silver years, this Bill represents a boost to financial security.

speaker: Mr Neil Parekh Nimil Rajnikant (Nominated Member)
text: It ensures that retirees can efficiently access their savings when they need them the most.

speaker: Mr Neil Parekh Nimil Rajnikant (Nominated Member)
text: This Bill also ensures that the provisions around clearer interest calculations and fund management foster greater trust in the CPF system, an essential element in preserving confidence in our social security infrastructure.

speaker: Mr Neil Parekh Nimil Rajnikant (Nominated Member)
text: These amendments can foster a more equitable labour market where workers have access to adequate retirement savings.

speaker: Mr Neil Parekh Nimil Rajnikant (Nominated Member)
text: This could enhance employee satisfaction and retention in the long run, benefiting businesses through reduced turnover and improved morale.

speaker: Mr Neil Parekh Nimil Rajnikant (Nominated Member)
text: This Bill is also a win for businesses.

speaker: Mr Neil Parekh Nimil Rajnikant (Nominated Member)
text: The clarified guidelines for managing CPF-related insurance schemes, including the HPS insurance scheme, offer greater transparency and simplicity for employers managing insurance on behalf of their employees.

speaker: Mr Neil Parekh Nimil Rajnikant (Nominated Member)
text: The streamlining of CPF account administration also makes it easier for employers to manage contributions and compliance.

speaker: Mr Neil Parekh Nimil Rajnikant (Nominated Member)
text: These, in turn, will reduce administrative burdens, allowing businesses to focus on their core operations.

speaker: Mr Neil Parekh Nimil Rajnikant (Nominated Member)
text: However, besides providing some benefits to our citizens and businesses, this Bill may lead to certain challenges.

speaker: Mr Neil Parekh Nimil Rajnikant (Nominated Member)
text: Will the members be notified beforehand and will they have options to manage their accounts before closure?

speaker: Mr Neil Parekh Nimil Rajnikant (Nominated Member)
text: Two, how will the closure of SAs affect ongoing payments or contributions linked to these accounts?

speaker: Mr Neil Parekh Nimil Rajnikant (Nominated Member)
text: Three, could the Minister provide more details on the formula for calculating interest on funds transferred from closed SAs?

speaker: Mr Neil Parekh Nimil Rajnikant (Nominated Member)
text: How extensive will this coverage be for those with pre-existing conditions?

speaker: Mr Neil Parekh Nimil Rajnikant (Nominated Member)
text: How will premium adjustments for members with pre-existing conditions be handled, and will there be an appeals process if members disagree with the risk assessments?

speaker: Mr Neil Parekh Nimil Rajnikant (Nominated Member)
text: Six, could the Minister elaborate on the specifics of the governance changes that simplify the constitution of the CPF Board and what is the potential impact of this change?

speaker: Mr Neil Parekh Nimil Rajnikant (Nominated Member)
text: What changes have been made on the criteria for appointing the Chairperson and Deputy Chairperson of the CPF Board and how these appointments will ensure the CPF Board operates efficiently?

speaker: Mr Neil Parekh Nimil Rajnikant (Nominated Member)
text: Together, these challenges will enhance both individual retirement readiness and the overall stability of Singapore’s workforce.

speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: This amendment marks a significant step towards ensuring greater financial security for Singaporeans, especially those with serious pre-existing health conditions.

speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: Currently, the HPS covers individuals in good health or with mild pre-existing conditions.

speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: However, as we continue to be more inclusive, it is crucial to explore how advances in medical technology can further enhance the scheme's scope.

speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: This brings me to my first point of incorporating medical advancements into HPS premiums.

speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: We can look to countries like Germany and Canada for reference, where insurers frequently revise premiums for chronic illnesses, such as cancer, factoring in breakthroughs like immunotherapy and targeted treatments.

speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: This ensures that premiums reflect the progress of medical treatments.

speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: Singapore could benefit from such a similar approach of adopting a more dynamic review process.

speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: By integrating the latest medical advancements, we ensure that individuals receiving such treatments pay HPS premiums that are reflective of their improved health outlook.

speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: Are there plans to incorporate advancements in medical treatments when revising premiums in such reviews?

speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: My third point is about premium adjustments for patients in remission.

speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: In countries, such as Australia and the United Kingdom (UK), patients in remission often see a reduction in their premiums after a period without recurrence, two years in Australia and three years in the UK.

speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: With this in mind, I would like to ask the Minister what is the current review period and if the Ministry is considering shortening the review period for HPS premium adjustments for members in remission.

speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: Offering such relief would acknowledge the efforts of those who have overcome serious health conditions and now maintain stable health.

speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: My fourth point is about broader risk pooling in national schemes.

speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: Countries like Sweden and Norway adopt an inclusive approach to risk pooling, spreading risks across the entire population.

speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: This significantly reduces the financial burden on high-risk individuals, making coverage more affordable for all.

speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: In Norway, for instance, the National Insurance Scheme provides automatic health coverage to all residents, including those with pre-existing conditions.

speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: MediShield Life provides an excellent example of how risk pooling can work effectively within a national scheme.

speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: It does so by spreading risks across a large pool, ensuring inclusivity for those with pre-existing conditions.

speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: While MediShield Life already covers individuals with pre-existing conditions, HPS has historically excluded those with more serious conditions.

speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: Can we adopt a similar model for HPS, broadening the risk pool to alleviate the premium burden on high-risk individuals?

speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: Doing so, we protect the potentially more vulnerable members of our society.

speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: My fifth point is about tiered coverage options for greater flexibility.

speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: In other countries, such as the United States and New Zealand, tiered insurance options allow individuals to choose lower coverage levels at reduced premiums.

speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: This flexibility is especially beneficial for high-risk individuals who may struggle to afford full coverage.

speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: This will provide individuals with serious pre-existing conditions the opportunity to opt for a lower coverage level at a more manageable premium, thus ensuring they are still protected within their financial means.

speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: This is with regard to Prime and Plus flat owners who purchase their flats from HDB.

speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: This subsidy recovery is proportionate to the extent of additional subsidies initially provided.

speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: One, the recovery of subsidies is premised on the flat being sold at a higher price than its purchase price.

speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: We should clarify the formulation of this refund in relation to the valuation at the time of sale, accounting for factors, such as lease depreciation, inflation and current market conditions.

speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: Two, in the event of a property market downturn, how will the recoverable subsidies be calculated?

speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: The real-term valuation which takes into account inflation at the point of sale may be lower than the original purchase price or the grant’s initial value.

speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: This could lead to complications in determining the appropriate amount of subsidy to recover.

speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: Hence, I seek the Minister to provide clarifications on the calculations concerning these two points.

speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: A transparent and fair approach to subsidy recovery, especially in fluctuating markets, will benefit both flat owners and the Government in maintaining clarity and fairness in the system.

speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: This is especially true in areas, such as the expansion of HPS.

speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: This is also an opportunity to make the scheme even more dynamic, inclusive and equitable, especially for those with pre-existing health conditions.

speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: I urge the Minister to consider the suggestions.

speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: Notwithstanding this, I reiterate my support for this Bill.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: I will first address questions related to the amendments to effect the closure of the SA for members aged 55 and above, followed by the expansion of HPS.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: As I have shared earlier on, these amendments are part of the evolution of the CPF system to continue serving the needs of Singaporeans over the course of their lives.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: With regard to the SA closure, Mr Neil Parekh asked about how affected CPF members will be notified of the SA closure and Mr Louis Ng also asked about the resources extended to CPF members.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: To help Members plan ahead, CPF Board has enhanced the Retirement Dashboard on their website.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: The dashboard allows members to view the estimated amounts that will be transferred from their SA to their RA and OA.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: Information is also available on the CPF website and across CPF Board's communication channels.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: Members who need further assistance can contact CPF Board directly.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: Mr Louis Ng asked about the circumstances under which a member's SA will not be closed upon reaching age 55.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: These circumstances relate mainly to CPF members who pass away shortly before turning 55.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: We will not close their SA to streamline the administrative process for transferring these monies out of the CPF, for example, as payments to the members' nominees.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: Mr Parekh also asked about how the SA closure affects the computation of interest as well as ongoing payments and contributions.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: These are questions which CPF members are also likely to have.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: There are frequently asked questions today on CPF Board's website on these topics to help members.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: The remaining SA savings which are withdrawable will be transferred to the OA to earn OA interest for that month.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: Members who wish to earn the RA interest and commit their savings for higher retirement payouts can opt to transfer their OA savings to their RA up to the ERS within the same month.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: If there are incoming CPF contributions to the SA, these will be allocated to the RA up to the FRS, either in cash or with a mixture of cash and property, and any remaining contributions in excess of FRS will be allocated to the OA and can be withdrawn.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: For ongoing payments, transition measures will be put in place after the SA has been closed to ensure that members aged 55 and above have sufficient time to make the necessary arrangements.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: Participating members will be notified by the CPF Board of the relevant changes to the schemes and their options moving forward.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: Mr Louis Ng also asked about how many members are expected to reach the FRS, following the transfer from the SA and if the Government will regularly share the number of members expected to reach the Basic, Full and Enhanced Retirement Sums.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: As the transferred SA balances are not high, this is not expected to change FRS attainment by much.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: The BRS and FRS attainment rates are published on the website of the CPF Board annually.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: We have also been sharing the retirement sum attainment rates with the House through the recent Committee of Supply debates.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: Assoc Prof Jamus Lim asked about what happens to members' SA investments after the SA closure, because he has alluded to the fact that it runs contrary to having some form of commitment that our members have been enjoying.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: After the SA has been closed, members can continue to hold their existing CPF Investment Scheme (CPFIS)-SA investments, until they decide to sell them or until they mature.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: Upon sale or maturity, the proceeds from the member's CPFIS-SA will be paid to their RA up to the FRS, with any remaining balance paid to their OA.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: Members may also continue to use their OA monies to invest under the CPFIS-OA and this is consistent with the approach for CPFIS today.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: Members need to have set aside their FRS after turning 55 before they can invest under CPFIS.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: We will notify members in advance so that they are aware of the available options.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: Not providing any special treatment for CPFIS is also consistent with how we are not grandfathering older cohorts for SA closure.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: To Assoc Prof Lim's point about retirement planning and how the cost of inflation has affected members and, thus, in a way, nudging them to consider stretching the CPF monies in terms of getting extra interest, I want to highlight that over the last five years, the Government has rolled out significant numbers of packages to support many of our residents in terms of addressing some of the cost of living issues.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: So, we have raised it to four times the BRS.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: Our members have the flexibility to either retain these savings in the OA for liquidity or invest in safe instruments, such as Singapore Government Securities through the CPFIS.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: Financially savvy members may also grow their savings outside the CPF system.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: In fact, those who are investment savvy may prefer to consider relevant commercial investment products or otherwise they can leave their monies in their RA to continue earning the higher long-term interest rate and receive higher retirement payouts.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: I find, in terms of the statistics, looking at the numbers, I do not think that this move was motivated because of this SA shielding, because only a minority of members and that statistics is also available, about 2% in 2021 could have chosen to do so.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: So, we have extensively discussed this on several occasions in this House.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: As such, I seek Assoc Prof Jamus Lim and also Members' understanding that I will not repeat the points that have been raised and addressed before.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: I am also very heartened, Mr Speaker, Sir, and Members of the House, that with the expansion of the HPS, this has been positively received.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: There were clarifications on the coverage, the extent of the coverage of the HPS, the necessity and impact of premium loading and the process for HPS premium reviews.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: Mr Louis Ng and Ms Jean See asked if HPS already covers members with pre-existing medical conditions and how they will be affected.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: Mr Ng, Mr Yip Hon Weng, Mr Neil Parekh and Ms See also asked for clarity on the types of conditions covered under the expanded HPS and how many additional members would benefit.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: This includes individuals who have fully recovered from a stroke for some time.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: It also covers those with early-stage cancer and have remained in remission for a period of time.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: Members who are already eligible today would pay the same standard premiums.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: Members who are already eligible today would pay the same standard premiums.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: They will not be affected by the expansion of the HPS and the premium loading.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: With the proposed expansion, more members with pre-existing health conditions may be considered for coverage with premium loading.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: However, some applicants will remain ineligible for HPS because their conditions are just too severe to be insurable.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: Overextending HPS coverage for members with significantly higher claim risks could negatively affect the sustainability of the HPS.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: This is also in line with industry best practices and ensures the sustainability of HPS for the general population.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: Mr Neil Parekh and Ms Jean See asked how premium loading for members with pre-existing conditions would be handled.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: As with industry practice, each application is assessed individually.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: This means that eligibility for HPS coverage is assessed based on each member's personal health risk profile, taking into account overall severity, prognosis and control of all of their medical conditions.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: Where required, CPF Board obtains relevant information from medical professionals to gain a comprehensive understanding of the members' health status.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: Mr Louis Ng and Ms Jean See asked if previously rejected HPS applicants will be notified that they can submit a new application to be considered again.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: In fact, the Board already conducts outreach to members whose health conditions might improve to invite them to reapply for HPS with a medical report on their current health condition.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: Mr Edward Chia also asked if the Ministry would introduce tiered coverage options within HPS.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: Similar to other HPS members today, those subject to premium loading can choose the extent of coverage by adjusting their share of HPS cover, as long as the co-owners' total cover add up to 100% of the outstanding housing loan.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: Participation for those subject to premium loading will also be on an opt-in basis.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: We regularly review HPS coverage and affordability and we will also study Mr Chia's suggestion.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: Mr Yip Hon Weng asked about the rationale for HPS premium loading for members with higher health risks and whether there are safeguards in place to prevent individuals from lower-income groups from being disproportionately affected.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: Instead of premium loading, Mr Chia asked if HPS can broaden the risk pool to reduce the premiums charged on higher-risk individuals.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: Today, all approved HPS applications are covered at a standard premium rate.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: With the expansion of HPS, the premium loading will apply to members with certain pre-existing health conditions that are not so severe and who previously would not have been eligible for cover.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: And the additional premiums will be commensurate with their higher claims likelihood.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: This is in line with industry practice and is necessary to keep the HPS scheme sustainable.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: Without premium loading, HPS premiums may need to rise across the board for all members, including for those in the lower-income groups, in order to cross-subsidise the higher claim rates by members with more serious conditions.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: For members facing financial hardship, their familial co-owners can help to pay outstanding premiums.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: CPF Board also extends the grace period for premium repayment based on member's circumstances.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: Should members require help with their mortgage loans, HDB will assess each case and provide assistance.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: This can include allowing members to temporarily reduce or defer their loan instalments or extend their loan tenure to reduce their monthly instalments.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: Mr Neil Parekh asked about the appeal process for members who disagree with their risk assessments.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: Mr Edward Chia and Ms Jean See asked about reviewing premiums for members in remission.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: Members subjected to premium loading who are looking to have their premiums revised, can submit a medical report on their current health condition.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: CPF Board will then assess their requests and adjust premiums accordingly.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: For members who have signed on and they are under the HPS cover, if they develop health conditions after they have already signed up for the coverage, they will see no changes to their premium as a result.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: The HPS cover can also be ported over if they are looking to purchase a new flat.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: Mr Yip Hon Weng and Mr Chia also asked about the process to review HPS premiums and Mr Chia also asked if advancements in medical treatment are taken into account when revising premiums.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: During the review, several factors are considered, including the market competitiveness of HPS premium rates so that HPS remains affordable to members.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: CPF Board also considers the sustainability of HPS premium rates by taking into account factors, such as the claims experience, projected investment returns as well as the overall financial health of the Home Protection Fund.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: For example, when there is significant improvement in health outcomes among the general population due to advancements in medical treatments, this will be reflected in the claims experience and factored in during the review process.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: The underlying assumptions are also validated by an external actuarial consultant to ensure robustness of the premium review.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: Mr Edward Chia asked for clarity and Assoc Prof Jamus Lim highlighted on potential gaps that could happen from the calculation of the subsidy recovery amounts when Prime and Plus flats are sold.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: The subsidy recovery percentage will be commensurate with the extent of the initial additional subsidy provided.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: This ensures fairness to other Standard flat buyers who did not enjoy the additional subsidies, who are, likewise, subjected to the vagaries of the market.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: The set of additional restrictions imposed on Plus and Prime flats helps to keep these flats in attractive locations affordable at the point of resale.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: Nonetheless, there are existing channels for businesses and employers to provide feedback.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: Looks like there are no clarifications for Dr Tan.      .
